decisions.choice: the eighth vision: four chariots sent out through the earth
decisions.reason: The last vision answers the first. In 1:8-11 horsemen patrolled the earth and found it at rest while Jerusalem lay in ruins. Here four chariots, drawn by horses of different colors, go out from the LORD's presence to the four quarters, and the one sent north brings the LORD's spirit to rest there (verse 8). The angel explains them as the four winds of heaven (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the two mountains of bronze: the gateway from the LORD's presence
alternatives: the two bronze pillars of the temple
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the mountains. The article, "the two mountains", suggests a place the hearer would know. The chariots come out from standing before the Lord of all the earth (verse 5), so the mountains seem to mark the entrance to his presence. Bronze suggests strength that cannot be broken. Some see a likeness to the two bronze pillars at the entrance of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:15-22), or to mountains where, in other ancient writings, the sun was pictured rising between two peaks.

decisions.choice: chariots: war chariots, the strongest force of an ancient army
decisions.reason: Horse-drawn chariots were the power of kings (Exodus 14:7; 1 Kings 10:26). Elisha's servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire around them (2 Kings 6:17). The chariots here are the LORD's forces, sent out to carry out his will.

decisions.choice: Again I looked up (B); I looked up again (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:1, Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for "lifted up my eyes".

decisions.choice: "des chars" at every level
decisions.reason: French "char" is the war chariot; "chariot" today is a cart.

decisions.choice: "carros"
decisions.reason: The war chariots are "carros", the word of the Spanish histories, at every level.

decisions.choice: "병거" (L, B); "전차" (R)
decisions.reason: "병거" is the familiar Bible word for a war chariot; Readable uses the everyday word "전차".

decisions.choice: "cỗ xe chiến mã" for the chariots
decisions.reason: "Xe chiến mã" is the most common published word for war chariots (Joshua 11:4); "cỗ" counts them.

decisions.reason: The angel explains where the chariots go (verses 6-8), but not what the colors mean, as in the first vision (1:8). The red horses are not mentioned again. Revelation 6:1-8 takes up horses of these colors for its four riders.

decisions.choice: "roux" for the red horses

decisions.choice: dappled: spotted or speckled
decisions.reason: The word is used of the spotted goats in Jacob's flocks (Genesis 31:10, 12). It describes a horse marked with patches or spots of color.

decisions.choice: strong ones: the horses of the fourth chariot are powerful
alternatives: a color, such as gray or piebald
decisions.reason: The word means strong. It stands after "dappled" with no "and", so it may describe the dappled horses, or all four teams. In verse 7 "the strong ones" are spoken of as if they were a group of their own, and some take the word as another color. The translation reads it as a further description of the fourth team.

decisions.choice: strong, spotted horses (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two descriptions together before the noun and says "spotted" for "dappled". Balanced says "powerful ones".

decisions.choice: "tordos" (L, B); "manchados" (R)
decisions.reason: The dappled coat is "tordo", the word for a spotted horse; R uses the plainer "manchados".

decisions.choice: what are these: the question asked in each vision
decisions.reason: Zechariah asks the same question as in 1:9, 2:2 and 4:4. This is the angel's last appearance.

decisions.choice: My lord, what are these? (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 4:4 at each level.

decisions.choice: "mon seigneur", lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: polite address to the angel; "Monsieur" jars for an angel and "Seigneur" would read as God.

decisions.choice: "Thưa chúa tôi" (L, B) / "Thưa ngài" (R) for "my lord" said to the angel, with no deity span
decisions.reason: 'Adoni is a polite address to a superior, as Joshua 5:14 and 1 Kings 18:7; lowercase "chúa tôi" keeps it apart from God. R's "thưa ngài" is plainer.

decisions.choice: "bwana wangu", polite address to the angel, with no deity span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the prophet addresses the angel with the respectful "bwana wangu"; at the start of a sentence it takes the ordinary capital. It is not the divine title.

decisions.choice: "내 주여" for the angel at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: Zechariah addresses the angel as "내 주여" (adoni), never "주님", which is kept for God; as recorded at 1:9 for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "mi señor" (L, B); "señor" (R), lowercase
decisions.reason: Zechariah calls the angel "mi señor" with tú, lowercase, as the term sheet sets for the angel in Daniel and Zechariah. The question keeps the Hebrew order and the wording of 1:9 and 4:4 at each level.

decisions.choice: the four winds of heaven: the winds from the four directions, the LORD's servants
decisions.reason: The word means wind or spirit. "The four winds of heaven" are the winds from the four quarters of the world (2:10; Jeremiah 49:36; Daniel 7:2), and Psalm 104:4 says that God makes the winds his messengers. Some read "spirits", heavenly beings, which fits the picture of servants presenting themselves before their Lord. Either way the chariots carry out God's will in every direction.

decisions.choice: presenting themselves before: standing before a king to receive orders
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the heavenly beings who present themselves before the LORD in Job 1:6 and 2:1. Like servants at a royal court, the chariots stand before their Lord and then go out to do what he commands.

decisions.choice: the Lord of all the earth
decisions.reason: The same title as in 4:14.

decisions.choice: the four winds of the heavens (L); of heaven (B, R); Lord, capitalized
decisions.reason: The picture of the winds is kept at every level, as set for the visions. The angel's explanation runs to the end of verse 6, where the quotation mark closes.

decisions.choice: "les quatre vents des cieux" (L), "du ciel" (B, R); "le Seigneur de toute la terre" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English and the meaning decision; the term sheet fixes "le Seigneur de toute la terre" (4:14).

decisions.choice: "los cuatro vientos de los cielos" (L); "del cielo" (B, R); "el Señor de toda la tierra"
decisions.reason: The wording follows Daniel 7:2 and Joshua 3:11 in Spanish; "Señor" is capitalized, as the title of God.

decisions.choice: "Chúa của cả trái đất", capitalised, with no span
decisions.reason: 'Adon here is God; the term sheet's form from Zechariah 4:14. "Đứng chầu" (B) is the court word for standing before a king to receive orders.

decisions.choice: "pepo nne za mbinguni" (the four winds of heaven)
decisions.reason: Hebrew "ruach" here is wind, as the term sheet's "upepo" for wind, in the plural "pepo"; the same phrase as the published Daniel 7:2 and Revelation 7:1. The footnoted meaning decision gives the reading "spirits".

decisions.choice: "온 땅의 주님"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for "the Lord of all the earth" [Rev 11:4]; the angel speaks of God with the honorific.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֞הּ הַסּוּסִ֣ים הַשְּׁחֹרִ֗ים יֹֽצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְהַלְּבָנִ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְהַ֨בְּרֻדִּ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: [The one] which [has] in it the horses the black [is] going out to [the] land of [the] north, and the white went out after them, and the dappled went out to the land of the south.

en.L: The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south."
en.B: The chariot pulled by the black horses is heading for the land of the north, the white horses have gone out after them, and the dappled horses have gone toward the land of the south."
en.R: The chariot with the black horses is going toward the north. The white horses are following them, and the spotted horses are going toward the south."

fr.L: Celui où [sont] les chevaux noirs sort vers le pays du nord, et les blancs sont sortis après eux, et les tachetés sont sortis vers le pays du midi. »
fr.B: Le char attelé des chevaux noirs part vers le pays du nord, les chevaux blancs sont partis à leur suite, et les chevaux tachetés sont partis vers le pays du midi. »
fr.R: Le char avec les chevaux noirs part vers le nord. Les chevaux blancs les suivent, et les chevaux tachetés partent vers le sud. »

es.B: El carro de los caballos negros va hacia la tierra del norte; los caballos blancos han salido tras ellos, y los tordos han salido hacia la tierra del sur».
es.R: El carro de los caballos negros va hacia el norte. Los caballos blancos los siguen, y los manchados van hacia el sur».

vi.L: [Cỗ xe] có những con ngựa ô thì đi ra đến xứ phương bắc, và những con ngựa bạch đã đi theo sau chúng, và những con ngựa đốm đã đi ra đến xứ phương nam."
vi.B: Cỗ xe do những con ngựa ô kéo đang đi về xứ phương bắc, những con ngựa bạch đã đi theo sau chúng, còn những con ngựa đốm đã đi về phía xứ phương nam."
vi.R: Cỗ xe có những con ngựa màu đen đang đi về phương bắc. Những con ngựa màu trắng đi theo sau chúng, còn những con ngựa đốm đang đi về phương nam."

sw.L: [Gari] lile lenye farasi weusi linatoka kwenda nchi ya kaskazini, na wale weupe wakatoka kuwafuata, na wale wenye madoadoa wakatoka kwenda nchi ya kusini."
sw.B: Gari linalovutwa na farasi weusi linakwenda nchi ya kaskazini, farasi weupe wametoka kuwafuata, na farasi wenye madoadoa wamekwenda kuelekea nchi ya kusini."
sw.R: Gari lenye farasi weusi linakwenda upande wa kaskazini. Farasi weupe wanawafuata, na farasi wenye madoadoa wanakwenda upande wa kusini."

ko.L: 검은 말들이 [끄는] 것은 북쪽 땅으로 나가고, 흰 말들은 그 뒤를 따라 나갔으며, 얼룩진 말들은 남쪽 땅으로 나갔다."
ko.B: 검은 말들이 끄는 병거는 북쪽 땅으로 가고 있고, 흰 말들은 그 뒤를 따라 나갔으며, 얼룩진 말들은 남쪽 땅을 향해 나갔다."
ko.R: 검은 말들이 끄는 전차는 북쪽으로 가고 있다. 흰 말들이 그 뒤를 따라가고, 점박이 말들은 남쪽으로 가고 있다."

decisions.choice: the white went out after them: the white horses follow the black to the north
alternatives: the white went out to the west
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "after them". The word for "behind" can also mean "west" (the Hebrews faced east to name directions), and with a slight change some read "to the west", so that the chariots go to the north, west and south. As the text stands, two chariots go north, toward Babylon, and one south. No chariot is said to go east, and the red horses are not mentioned.

decisions.choice: the land of the north ... the land of the south: Babylon and Egypt
decisions.reason: The north is the direction from which Babylon's armies came and to which Judah was exiled (2:10). The south is the land of Egypt, the other great power. The chariots go out to the lands that had held God's people.

decisions.choice: The chariot (B, R); horses (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the one in which are the black horses" and then names the other teams only by color. Balanced and Readable add "chariot" and "horses" for clarity. The closing mark ends the angel's words begun in verse 5.

source.text: וְהָאֲמֻצִּ֣ים יָצְא֗וּ וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ לְהִתְהַלֵּ֣ךבָּאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְכ֖וּ הִתְהַלְּכ֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וַתִּתְהַלַּ֖כְנָה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the strong went out, and they sought to go, to go about in the earth; and he said, Go, go about in the earth. And they went about in the earth.

en.L: And the strong ones went out, and they sought to go to walk about through the earth; and he said, "Go, walk about through the earth." And they walked about through the earth.
en.B: When the powerful horses came out, they were eager to set off and patrol the earth. He said, "Go, patrol the earth!" So they patrolled the earth.
en.R: When the strong horses came out, they wanted to go and travel all over the earth. He said, "Go and travel all over the earth!" So they went all over the earth.

fr.L: Et les vigoureux sortirent, et ils cherchaient à aller parcourir la terre ; et il dit : « Allez, parcourez la terre. » Et ils parcoururent la terre.
fr.B: Quand les chevaux vigoureux sortirent, ils étaient impatients de partir pour patrouiller sur la terre. Il leur dit : « Allez, patrouillez sur la terre ! » Et ils patrouillèrent sur la terre.
fr.R: Quand les chevaux forts sont sortis, ils voulaient partir parcourir toute la terre. Il leur a dit : « Allez parcourir toute la terre ! » Alors ils sont partis à travers toute la terre.

es.L: Y los vigorosos salieron, y procuraban ir a recorrer la tierra; y él dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan, recorran|Id, recorred}} la tierra». Y recorrieron la tierra.
es.B: Cuando salieron los caballos fuertes, estaban deseosos de partir para patrullar la tierra. Él dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a patrullar la tierra!». Y patrullaron la tierra.
es.R: Cuando salieron los caballos fuertes, querían ir a recorrer toda la tierra. Él les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a recorrer toda la tierra!». Y la recorrieron por completo.

vi.L: Những con mạnh mẽ đi ra, và chúng tìm cách đi qua lại khắp đất; và người nói: "Hãy đi, đi qua lại khắp đất." Và chúng đi qua lại khắp đất.
vi.B: Khi những con ngựa mạnh mẽ đi ra, chúng nóng lòng lên đường đi tuần tra khắp đất. Người bảo: "Hãy đi tuần tra khắp đất!" Vậy chúng đi tuần tra khắp đất.
vi.R: Khi những con ngựa khỏe mạnh đi ra, chúng muốn đi khắp đất. Người bảo: "Hãy đi khắp đất!" Vậy chúng đi khắp đất.

sw.L: Nao wale wenye nguvu wakatoka, wakataka kwenda kutembea huku na huko duniani; naye akasema, "Nendeni, tembeeni huku na huko duniani." Nao wakatembea huku na huko duniani.
sw.B: Farasi wale wenye nguvu walipotoka, walikuwa na hamu ya kwenda kuizunguka dunia na kuilinda. Akasema, "Nendeni, mkaizunguke dunia!" Basi wakaizunguka dunia.
sw.R: Farasi wale wenye nguvu walipotoka, walitaka kwenda kusafiri pote duniani. Akasema, "Nendeni mkasafiri pote duniani!" Basi wakaenda pote duniani.

ko.L: 힘센 말들이 나가서 땅을 두루 다니려고 하자, 그가 말했다. "가서 땅을 두루 다녀라." 그러자 그것들이 땅을 두루 다녔다.
ko.B: 힘센 말들이 나와서 어서 가서 땅을 순찰하려고 하자, 그가 말했다. "가서 땅을 순찰하여라!" 그러자 그것들이 땅을 순찰했다.
ko.R: 힘센 말들이 나와서 온 세상을 돌아다니고 싶어 했다. 그러자 그가 말했다. "가서 온 세상을 돌아다녀라!" 그래서 그 말들이 온 세상을 돌아다녔다.

decisions.choice: walk about through the earth: patrol the earth, as the horsemen did in 1:10-11
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the horsemen of the first vision. The horses strain to go, and are given leave.

decisions.choice: the strong ones: the horses of the fourth chariot, or all the teams; he: the LORD or the angel
decisions.reason: "The strong ones" may be the dappled horses of verse 3 or the whole company of horses. The one who says "Go" is not named; it may be the Lord of all the earth, before whom they stood (verse 5), or the angel speaking for him.

decisions.choice: walk about (L); patrol (B); travel all over (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in 1:10-11 at each level, so the reader can see the link between the first and the last vision.

decisions.choice: "parcourir" (L, R), "patrouiller" (B)
decisions.reason: French "se promener" would sound idle; "parcourir" keeps the verb of going about, "patrouiller" follows the English Balanced.

decisions.choice: "recorrer" (L, R); "patrullar" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the horsemen's patrol of 1:10-11; the order to the teams is plural and takes plural_you.

decisions.choice: "kutembea huku na huko" (L); "kuizunguka dunia" (B); "kusafiri pote" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the walking of the Hebrew; Balanced gives the sense of patrolling, as the horsemen of 1:10-11; Readable says simply that they travel everywhere.

decisions.choice: "đi qua lại khắp đất" (L) / "đi tuần tra khắp đất" (B) / "đi khắp đất" (R), as 1:10-11
decisions.reason: The horses patrol the earth as the horsemen of 1:10-11, and the same Hebrew takes the same wording at each level; "tuần tra" is the word for a patrol. The speaker ("người", lowercase, who "bảo" rather than "phán") may be the LORD or the angel, so no deity span.

source.text: וַיַּזְעֵ֣ק אֹתִ֔י וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר רְאֵ֗ה הַיּֽוֹצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן הֵנִ֥יחוּ אֶת־רוּחִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, See, those going out to [the] land of [the] north have caused to rest my spirit in [the] land of [the] north.

en.L: And he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those going out to the land of the north have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit at rest in the land of the north."
en.B: Then he called out to me, "Look, those going toward the land of the north have given {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} spirit rest in the land of the north."
en.R: Then he called out to me, "Look! The ones going toward the north have calmed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against the land of the north."

fr.L: Et il m’appela à grands cris et me parla, disant : « Vois, ceux qui sortent vers le pays du nord ont fait reposer {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esprit dans le pays du nord. »
fr.B: Puis il m’appela à grands cris : « Regarde, ceux qui partent vers le pays du nord ont apaisé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esprit dans le pays du nord. »
fr.R: Puis il m’a appelé en criant : « Regarde ! Ceux qui partent vers le nord ont calmé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère contre le pays du nord. »

es.L: Y me llamó a gritos y me habló, diciendo: «Mira, los que salen hacia la tierra del norte han hecho reposar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu en la tierra del norte».
es.B: Entonces me llamó en voz alta: «Mira, los que van hacia la tierra del norte han dado reposo a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espíritu en la tierra del norte».
es.R: Entonces me llamó en voz alta: «¡Mira! Los que van hacia el norte han calmado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo contra la tierra del norte».

vi.L: Rồi người gọi lớn với tôi và nói với tôi rằng: "Hãy xem, những con đi ra đến xứ phương bắc đã làm cho thần của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yên nghỉ trong xứ phương bắc."
vi.B: Rồi người gọi tôi và nói: "Hãy xem, những con đi về xứ phương bắc đã làm cho thần của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được yên nghỉ tại xứ phương bắc."
vi.R: Rồi người gọi tôi và nói: "Hãy xem! Những con ngựa đi về phương bắc đã làm nguôi cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối với xứ phương bắc."

sw.L: Kisha akanililia, akasema nami, akisema, "Tazama, wale wanaotoka kwenda nchi ya kaskazini wameituliza roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika nchi ya kaskazini."
sw.B: Kisha akaniita kwa sauti, "Tazama, wale wanaokwenda kuelekea nchi ya kaskazini wameipa roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} pumziko katika nchi ya kaskazini."
sw.R: Kisha akaniita kwa sauti, "Tazama! Wale wanaokwenda upande wa kaskazini wameituliza hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} dhidi ya nchi ya kaskazini."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 나에게 외쳐 말했다. "보아라, 북쪽 땅으로 나가는 것들이 북쪽 땅에서 내 영을 쉬게 하였다."
ko.B: 그때 그가 나를 불러 말했다. "보아라, 북쪽 땅으로 가는 것들이 북쪽 땅에서 내 영을 쉬게 했다."
ko.R: 그때 그가 나를 불러 말했다. "보아라! 북쪽으로 가는 것들이 북쪽 땅을 향한 내 분노를 가라앉혔다."

decisions.choice: he cried out to me: the speaker voices the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named, but he says "my spirit", which is the LORD's. Either the LORD himself speaks, or the angel speaks in his name. Either way, the words are the LORD's.

decisions.choice: set my spirit at rest: my anger has been satisfied
alternatives: have placed my Spirit on the land of the north, stirring the exiles to return
decisions.reason: The word for spirit can mean anger or passion (Judges 8:3; Ecclesiastes 10:4), and Ezekiel uses a similar phrase for God's wrath coming to rest after it has done its work (Ezekiel 5:13; 16:42; 24:13). Read that way, the chariots have carried out judgment on Babylon, and the LORD's anger is at rest. Others read it as God's Spirit set on the north, stirring the exiles there to come home (compare Ezra 1:1, 5), which leads well into verse 10. The translation follows the first reading; the Hebrew could carry either.

decisions.choice: rest: the visions end with the LORD's purpose fulfilled
decisions.reason: The first vision found the nations at rest while Jerusalem lay in ruins and the LORD was angry with them (1:11, 15). The last ends with the LORD's own spirit at rest, because his judgment on the north has been carried out.

decisions.choice: spirit, lowercase (L, B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: The word here means God's inner feeling, his anger (m2), not his Spirit as a person, so it is lowercase; Readable says "anger". "My" takes the setting for pronouns of God. Balanced and Readable leave out the repeated "spoke to me, saying".

decisions.choice: "esprit", lowercase (L, B), "colère" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: God's spirit here is his anger; the capital, which French uses for God's Spirit, is in the English footnote.

decisions.choice: "espíritu", lowercase (L, B); "enojo" (R)
decisions.reason: Ruach here is God's anger, as the meaning decision reads it, so it stays lowercase at L and B and becomes "enojo" at R, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "thần của Ta", lowercase (L, B) / "cơn giận của Ta" (R)
decisions.reason: Ruach here is God's anger; lowercase "thần" keeps it from being read as the Spirit ("Thần Linh"), as the English keeps "spirit" lowercase.

decisions.choice: "roho yangu", lowercase (L, B); "hasira yangu" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: "ruach" here is God's anger, so it is not capitalized as the Spirit; Readable says "hasira" (anger). The footnoted meaning decision gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: "내 영" (L, B); "내 분노" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: spirit here is God's anger (term sheet), so Readable says "분노"; the speaker voices God and takes no -시-.

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.B: Puis la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

es.B: Entonces la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a mí:
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dio este mensaje:

vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho tôi sứ điệp này:

decisions.choice: a new message after the visions: a sign with crowns
decisions.reason: The visions are over. The word that follows tells Zechariah to perform a sign: to make a crown from the exiles' gifts and set it on the high priest's head, as a pledge of the Branch who will build the temple (verses 10-15).

decisions.choice: the formula as in 4:8
decisions.reason: The wording set for the prophets, as in 4:8.

decisions.choice: "La parole du SEIGNEUR me fut adressée, disant :" (L), "... me fut adressée :" (B), "Le SEIGNEUR m'a donné ce message :" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as the term sheet and published Jeremiah 1:4.

decisions.choice: "Vino a mí la palabra del SEÑOR, diciendo:" (L); "La palabra del SEÑOR vino a mí:" (B); "El SEÑOR me dio este mensaje:" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the Spanish of Jeremiah 1:4 at each level, through Zechariah.

decisions.choice: "Lời CHÚA đến với tôi rằng:" / "... đến với tôi:" / "CHÚA ban cho tôi sứ điệp này:"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's formula, as Isaiah and Jeremiah; the oracle that follows has no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "Neno la BWANA likanijia, kusema:" (L); "Neno la BWANA likanijia:" (B); "BWANA alinipa ujumbe huu:" (R)
decisions.reason: The formula of the term sheet, as the published Jeremiah 1:4. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: The term sheets' formula for "the word of the LORD came to me" at each level
decisions.reason: Recorded once for all of Zechariah; it ends in a period, not the English colon.

source.text: לָק֨וֹחַ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מֵחֶלְדַּ֕י וּמֵאֵ֥ת טוֹבִיָּ֖ה וּמֵאֵ֣ת יְדַֽעְיָ֑ה וּבָאתָ֤ אַתָּה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּבָ֗אתָ בֵּ֚ית יֹאשִׁיָּ֣ה בֶן־צְפַנְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖אוּ מִבָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Take from the exiles, from Heldai and from Tobiah and from Jedaiah, and come you on the day that, and come [to the] house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who have come from Babylon.

en.L: Take from the exiles, from Heldai, from Tobiah and from Jedaiah, and you, go on that same day, go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, they who have come from Babylon.
en.B: Take a gift from the exiles Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah, who have just come from Babylon, and on that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
en.R: Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah have come back from exile in Babylon. Take a gift from them, and on that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

fr.L: Prends de la part des exilés, de Heldaï, de Tobiya et de Yedaya, et va, toi, en ce jour-là, va à la maison de Josias fils de Sophonie, eux qui sont venus de Babylone.
fr.B: Reçois un don des exilés Heldaï, Tobiya et Yedaya, qui viennent d’arriver de Babylone, et ce jour-là, va à la maison de Josias fils de Sophonie.
fr.R: Heldaï, Tobiya et Yedaya sont revenus de l’exil à Babylone. Prends le don qu’ils apportent, et le jour même, va à la maison de Josias fils de Sophonie.

es.L: Toma de los del destierro, de Heldai, de Tobías y de Jedaías, y ve tú en ese mismo día, ve a la casa de Josías hijo de Sofonías, ellos que han venido de Babilonia.
es.B: Toma una ofrenda de los desterrados Heldai, Tobías y Jedaías, que acaban de llegar de Babilonia, y ese mismo día ve a la casa de Josías hijo de Sofonías.
es.R: Heldai, Tobías y Jedaías han llegado del destierro en Babilonia. Recibe de ellos una ofrenda, y ese mismo día ve a la casa de Josías hijo de Sofonías.

vi.L: Hãy nhận từ những người lưu đày, từ Hên-đai, từ Tô-bi-gia và từ Giê-đa-gia; và chính ngươi, ngay trong ngày ấy, hãy đi, hãy đến nhà Giô-si-a con trai Sô-phô-ni, là những người đã từ Ba-by-lôn đến.
vi.B: Hãy nhận lễ vật từ những người lưu đày là Hên-đai, Tô-bi-gia và Giê-đa-gia, những người vừa từ Ba-by-lôn đến; rồi ngay trong ngày ấy, con hãy đi đến nhà Giô-si-a con trai Sô-phô-ni.
vi.R: Hên-đai, Tô-bi-gia và Giê-đa-gia đã từ chốn lưu đày ở Ba-by-lôn trở về. Con hãy nhận lễ vật từ họ, và ngay trong ngày ấy, hãy đi đến nhà Giô-si-a con trai Sô-phô-ni.

sw.L: Chukua kutoka kwa watu wa uhamisho, kutoka kwa Heldai, na kwa Tobia, na kwa Yedaya, nawe uende siku hiyo hiyo, uende nyumbani kwa Yosia mwana wa Sefania, wao waliokuja kutoka Babeli.
sw.B: Pokea zawadi kutoka kwa watu wa uhamishoni, Heldai, Tobia na Yedaya, ambao wamekuja karibuni kutoka Babeli, na siku hiyo hiyo uende nyumbani kwa Yosia mwana wa Sefania.
sw.R: Heldai, Tobia na Yedaya wamerudi kutoka uhamishoni Babeli. Pokea zawadi kutoka kwao, na siku hiyo hiyo uende nyumbani kwa Yosia mwana wa Sefania.

ko.L: 포로들에게서, 헬대와 도비야와 여다야에게서 받아라. 그리고 너는 바로 그날 가서, 스바냐의 아들 요시야의 집으로 들어가거라. 그들이 바빌론에서 왔다.
ko.B: 포로로 가 있던 사람들, 곧 바빌론에서 막 돌아온 헬대와 도비야와 여다야에게서 예물을 받아라. 그리고 바로 그날 스바냐의 아들 요시야의 집으로 가거라.
ko.R: 헬대와 도비야와 여다야가 포로로 살던 바빌론에서 돌아왔다. 그들에게서 예물을 받아라. 그리고 바로 그날 스바냐의 아들 요시야의 집으로 가거라.

decisions.choice: the exiles: Jews still living in Babylon, who sent gifts to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "The exile" is the name for the community of Jews taken to Babylon and their descendants. Many stayed there after the return began, and sent silver and gold for the temple (Ezra 1:4, 6; 7:15-16; 8:25-30). Heldai, Tobiah and Jedaiah seem to have brought such gifts.

decisions.choice: take ... who have come from Babylon: take the silver and gold the three men have brought
alternatives: Josiah's household, who have come from Babylon
decisions.reason: "Take" has no object until verse 11, which names silver and gold. "Who have come" is plural, so it most likely refers to the three men, who may be staying in Josiah's house. It could refer to Josiah's household. The Hebrew joins the clauses loosely; the sense is clear enough.

decisions.choice: a gift (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is to be taken, which verse 11 makes plain. They put "who have arrived from Babylon" next to the three men. Literal keeps the Hebrew order and "you, go".

decisions.choice: Heldaï, Tobiya, Yedaya, Josias fils de Sophonie
decisions.reason: The names as the term sheet, in the forms of the published Chronicles and Ezra.

decisions.choice: "los del destierro" (L); "los desterrados" (B); "del destierro" (R)
decisions.reason: The exiles (golah) are named with "destierro", the word of the Spanish histories and of Ezra.

decisions.choice: "una ofrenda"
decisions.reason: B and R supply what is taken, the silver and gold of verse 11, as the English does.

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) to the prophet
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address for God's commissions to Zechariah: "ngươi" at L, "con" at B and R.

decisions.choice: names "Hên-đai" (1 Chronicles 27:15), "Tô-bi-gia", "Giê-đa-gia", "Giô-si-a con trai Sô-phô-ni"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; Josiah and Zephaniah keep the published spellings of the king and the prophet.

decisions.choice: "Heldai", "Tobia", "Yedaya", "Yosia mwana wa Sefania"
decisions.reason: The published Swahili forms of these names (1 Chronicles 27:15; Ezra 2:36, 60; Jeremiah 21:1). This Josiah is not the king, as his father's name shows.

decisions.choice: "예물" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English "a gift": what is taken is the silver and gold of verse 11 (meaning decision).

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ כֶֽסֶף־וְזָהָ֖ב וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עֲטָר֑וֹת וְשַׂמְתָּ֗ בְּרֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֥ן הַגָּדֽוֹל׃

en.L: And take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set [it] on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
en.B: Take the silver and gold and make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.

vi.L: Hãy lấy bạc và vàng, làm những mão miện, và đặt [nó] trên đầu Giô-suê con trai Giê-hô-xa-đác, thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm.

sw.L: Nawe chukua fedha na dhahabu, ufanye mataji, uweke juu ya kichwa cha Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu.
sw.B: Chukua fedha na dhahabu, utengeneze taji, uiweke juu ya kichwa cha Yoshua mwana wa Yehosadaki, kuhani mkuu.

ko.L: 은과 금을 받아 면류관들을 만들고, [그것을] 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아의 머리에 씌워라.
ko.B: 그 은과 금을 받아 면류관을 만들어, 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아의 머리에 씌워라.
ko.R: 그 은과 금을 가지고 왕관을 만들어라. 그리고 그것을 여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아의 머리에 씌워라.

decisions.choice: crowns: one crown made of several rings, or a crown of silver and one of gold
alternatives: two crowns, one for Joshua and one for the Branch
decisions.reason: The word is plural, but in verse 14 it takes a singular verb ("the crowns will be"), and only one head is named. The plural may mean one splendid crown made of several circlets (compare Revelation 19:12, "many crowns"), or two crowns, of which only one is set on Joshua. The translation reads one crown at the levels that do not keep the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Jehozadak: the high priest of chapter 3
decisions.reason: His father Jehozadak was taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 5:41). In Ezra he is called Jeshua son of Jozadak; see the note at Haggai 1:1.

decisions.choice: the crown set on the high priest: a sign pointing to the Branch
decisions.reason: Kings, not priests, wore crowns. Joshua is crowned as a sign, as he and his fellow priests were called "men of a sign" in 3:8, pointing to "a man whose name is the Branch" (verse 12). Because the Branch is a king of David's line, some have suggested that the crown was first meant for Zerubbabel, but no manuscript names him here. The text as it stands joins priest and king in one sign (verse 13).

decisions.choice: crowns (L); a crown (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plural form; Balanced and Readable say "a crown", following the singular verb of verse 14 (m1).

decisions.choice: "Josué fils de Yehotsadaq, le grand prêtre"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: Zechariah keeps the Hebrew of Haggai, while Ezra keeps "Yeshoua"; "grand prêtre" with no hyphen as the style guide.

decisions.choice: "Josué hijo de Josadac"
decisions.reason: The high priest is "Josué" in Haggai and Zechariah, as the English keeps "Joshua"; Ezra's "Jesúa" is the same man. "Josadac" is the published form.

decisions.choice: "những mão miện" (L) / "một mão miện" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Mão miện" is the published Bible word for a crown (Revelation 9:7); "vương miện" would say outright that it is a king's crown, which the sign only points to.

decisions.choice: "mataji" (L) for the plural "crowns"; "taji" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Taji" is the same in singular and plural, so Literal uses the plural form "mataji" to keep the Hebrew plural visible; Balanced and Readable follow the English "a crown".

decisions.choice: "면류관들" (L), "면류관" (B), "왕관" (R); "여호사닥의 아들 대제사장 여호수아"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plural is kept at Literal, one crown at B and R as the English (meaning decision). Joshua's name follows the term sheet for Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra has 요사닥의 아들 예수아).

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה־אִ֞ישׁ צֶ֤מַח שְׁמוֹ֙ וּמִתַּחְתָּ֣יו יִצְמָ֔ח וּבָנָ֖ה אֶת־הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to him, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: Look, a man, Branch [is] his name, and from under him he will sprout, and he will build the temple of Yahweh.

en.L: And say to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Look, a man whose name [is] the Branch! And from his place he will branch out, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Say to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will branch out from his place, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Tell him, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will grow up from his own place, and he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Et dis-lui : Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Voici un homme dont le nom [est] Germe ! Et de dessous lui il germera, et il bâtira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Dis-lui : {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Voici l’homme dont le nom est le Germe. Il germera de sa place, et il bâtira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Dis-lui : Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Voici l’homme qui s’appelle le Germe. Il poussera à partir de l’endroit où il est, et il construira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

es.L: Y dile: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: He aquí un hombre cuyo nombre [es] Retoño; y de su lugar retoñará, y edificará el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Dile: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Este es el hombre cuyo nombre es Retoño. Retoñará desde su lugar y edificará el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Dile: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Aquí está el hombre cuyo nombre es Retoño. Él crecerá desde su propio lugar y construirá el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Hãy nói với người rằng: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Kìa, một người có tên [là] Chồi! Người sẽ nẩy chồi từ chỗ mình, và người sẽ xây đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Con hãy nói với người: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Đây là người có tên là Chồi. Người sẽ nẩy chồi từ chỗ mình, và người sẽ xây đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Hãy nói với người: "Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Đây là người có tên là Chồi. Người sẽ mọc lên từ chính chỗ mình, và người sẽ xây đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

sw.L: Nawe umwambie, ukisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Tazama, mtu ambaye jina lake [ni] Chipukizi! Naye atachipuka kutoka mahali pake, naye atajenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mwambie, "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Huyu hapa ndiye mtu ambaye jina lake ni Chipukizi. Atachipuka kutoka mahali pake, naye atajenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mwambie, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Huyu hapa ndiye mtu ambaye jina lake ni Chipukizi. Atakua kutoka mahali pake mwenyewe, naye atajenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그에게 말하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 보라, 그 이름이 싹인 사람이다! 그가 자기 자리에서 싹터 나와, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 것이다.
ko.B: 그에게 말하여라. "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 이름이 싹인 사람이 여기 있다. 그가 자기 자리에서 싹터 나와 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 것이다.
ko.R: 그에게 말하여라. "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 이름이 싹인 사람이 여기 있다. 그는 자기가 있는 곳에서 싹이 돋듯 자라나서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 것이다.

decisions.choice: a man whose name is the Branch: the coming king promised in 3:8
decisions.reason: See the note at 3:8. "Look, a man" may point to Joshua as the sign, but the Branch is spoken of as another person, who will build the temple and rule (verse 13). Zerubbabel, of David's line, had begun the temple and was to finish it (4:9), and many readers see him here. Jewish tradition read the Branch as the Messiah, and Christians see the promise fulfilled in Jesus. The text names him by his title only.

decisions.choice: from his place he will branch out: a play on his name
decisions.reason: The verb "branch out" or "sprout" comes from the same root as "Branch". "From under him" means from where he stands, from his own roots: he will spring up in the land, not be brought in from outside.

decisions.choice: the temple: the LORD's house, the palace of the divine King
decisions.reason: The word means a palace or great house, and is used for the LORD's temple (Haggai 2:15, 18). The Branch will build it.

decisions.choice: the Branch, capitalized; branch out (L, B); grow up (R); no deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in 3:8 and Jeremiah 23:5, "Branch" is capitalized at every level. Literal and Balanced say "branch out" to keep the play on the name; Readable says "grow up". The Branch takes no deity_pronoun setting, as Isaiah's servant does not. The words Zechariah is to say are in double quotation marks and close at the end of verse 13.

decisions.choice: "le Germe", capitalised, with "il germera" (L, B), "il poussera" (R); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and published Jeremiah 23:5; French "germe ... germera" keeps the play on the name that the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR des armées :" (L), "Le SEIGNEUR des armées dit ceci :" (B), "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR des armées :" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as the term sheet; the message the prophet is told to deliver takes no quotation marks (to 6:13), as the term sheet sets for French, where the English quotes it.

decisions.choice: "Retoño", capitalized; "retoñará" (L, B); "crecerá" (R)
decisions.reason: The Branch is "Retoño" as in Jeremiah 23:5 and 33:15 in Spanish; the verb "retoñar" keeps the play on the name at L and B. The man takes no deity_pronoun span, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "Así dice el SEÑOR de los ejércitos:" (L); "El SEÑOR de los Ejércitos dice esto:" (B); "Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos:" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula follows the Spanish prophets at each level.

decisions.choice: "Chồi", capitalised, with "nẩy chồi" (L, B) / "mọc lên" (R); the man is "người", lowercase, with no deity span
decisions.reason: The term sheet's "Chồi" (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8). The verb "nẩy chồi" keeps the play on the name at L and B.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán thế này:" / "... phán như vầy:" / "Đây là lời CHÚA Vạn Quân phán:"
alternatives: "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" at every level
decisions.reason: Koh 'amar takes the three-level formula of Isaiah and Jeremiah; plain "phán" is kept for 'amar after an oracle.

decisions.choice: "Chipukizi", capitalized, and "atachipuka" (L, B); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and the published Jeremiah 23:5: the Branch is a title, and the verb from the same root ("atachipuka") keeps the play on his name at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "atakua" (he will grow), as the English.

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi asema hivi:" (L); "Hivi ndivyo BWANA wa majeshi asemavyo:" (B); "Hili ndilo BWANA wa majeshi analosema:" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula of the term sheet, as the published Isaiah, Jeremiah and Haggai. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "싹" and "싹터 나와" (L, B); "싹이 돋듯 자라나서" (R); no -시- for the Branch
decisions.reason: The Branch is "싹" as in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Zechariah 3:8 (term sheet); the verb keeps the play on his name. The English has no deity span for him, so he takes no honorific.

decisions.choice: "만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L); "이렇게 말씀하신다" (B); "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheets' "Thus says the LORD of hosts", ending in a period; recorded once for all of Zechariah.

records.literal_gloss: And he will build the temple of Yahweh, and he will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and there will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.

en.L: Yes, he will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he will bear majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne; and there will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them."
en.B: It is he who will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he will be clothed with majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne. There will be a priest on his throne, and the two of them will be in peaceful agreement."
en.R: He is the one who will build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He will be given royal honor, and he will sit on his throne and rule. And there will be a priest on his throne. The two of them will work together in peace."

fr.L: Oui, lui, il bâtira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et lui, il portera la majesté, et il siégera et dominera sur son trône ; et il y aura un prêtre sur son trône, et un conseil de paix sera entre eux deux.
fr.B: C’est lui qui bâtira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; il sera revêtu de majesté, il siégera sur son trône et gouvernera. Un prêtre siégera sur son trône, et une parfaite entente régnera entre eux deux.
fr.R: C’est lui qui construira le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il recevra les honneurs d’un roi, il s’assiéra sur son trône et il gouvernera. Un prêtre aussi sera sur son trône. Les deux travailleront ensemble dans la paix.

es.L: Sí, él edificará el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y él llevará majestad, y se sentará y gobernará sobre su trono; y habrá un sacerdote sobre su trono, y habrá consejo de paz entre los dos».

vi.R: Chính người là người sẽ xây đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Người sẽ được ban vinh dự của bậc vua chúa, và sẽ ngồi trên ngai mà cai trị. Cũng sẽ có một thầy tế lễ trên ngai. Hai người sẽ cùng làm việc với nhau trong hòa bình."

ko.L: 그렇다, 그가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 것이고, 그가 위엄을 지니고 자기 왕좌에 앉아 다스릴 것이다. 또 자기 왕좌에 제사장이 있을 것이며, 그 둘 사이에 평화의 의논이 있을 것이다."

ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 사람은 바로 그이다. 그는 왕의 영예를 받고, 왕좌에 앉아 다스릴 것이다. 그리고 그의 왕좌에 제사장도 있을 것이다. 그 두 사람은 평화롭게 함께 일할 것이다."

decisions.choice: he will build: stress on the one who builds
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "he" and the promise of verse 12, to stress that this man, and no other, will build the LORD's temple.

decisions.choice: majesty: royal splendor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the honor and glory of kings (Psalm 21:6; 45:4; Jeremiah 22:18). The Branch will bear it as a king.

decisions.choice: there will be a priest on his throne: a priest will sit on a throne beside the king
alternatives: he will be a priest on his throne (the king himself will also be a priest)
a priest will stand at his right hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read in two ways. "He will be a priest on his throne" makes the Branch himself both king and priest, and the two in the last clause would be his two offices; this reading is often joined to Psalm 110:4 and to Hebrews 7. Or "there will be a priest on his throne", that is, a priest will sit on a throne of his own, and "the two of them", king and priest, will act in harmony. The Greek translation reads "a priest at his right hand". The translation keeps the Hebrew words so that both readings remain open; the mention of "the two of them" fits the second best.

decisions.choice: a counsel of peace between them: full agreement in their plans
decisions.reason: "Counsel" means plans or purpose. King and priest, or the two offices joined in one man, will act together without rivalry.

decisions.choice: Yes, he (L); It is he who (B); He is the one who (R); be clothed with majesty (B); be given royal honor (R)
decisions.reason: Each level marks the stress of the repeated "he" (m1). Balanced says "be clothed with majesty", a common picture for bearing royal glory, and Readable says what majesty means. The pronouns for the Branch take no deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "une parfaite entente régnera entre eux deux" (B) for a counsel of peace
decisions.reason: Following the meaning decision (full agreement in their plans); Literal keeps "un conseil de paix".

ko.B: 그 면류관은 헬렘과 도비야와 여다야와 스바냐의 아들 헨을 기념하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 보관될 것이다.
ko.R: 그 왕관은 헬렘과 도비야와 여다야와 스바냐의 아들 헨을 기억하게 하려고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 보관될 것이다.

decisions.choice: Helem and Hen: other names for Heldai and Josiah of verse 10
alternatives: Hen as a word: by the kindness of the son of Zephaniah
decisions.reason: Helem seems to be another form of the name Heldai (verse 10). Hen is a word meaning "favor" or "kindness", and stands where Josiah son of Zephaniah stood in verse 10; it may be another name for him, or the phrase may mean "for the kindness of the son of Zephaniah", who received the men in his house. The Syriac translation reads Heldai and Josiah, as in verse 10. This description of the Syriac is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: a memorial: something kept before the LORD as a reminder
decisions.reason: Things kept "as a memorial" in the sanctuary reminded God and the people of something (Exodus 28:12, 29; 30:16; Numbers 31:54). The crown, laid up in the temple, would recall the gift of the exiles and the promise of the Branch until it was fulfilled.

decisions.choice: The crown (B, R); kept in the temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Balanced and Readable read one crown. They add "kept" to make the sense of a memorial "in the temple" plain. Literal keeps the plural.

decisions.choice: "Hélem" and "Hen" as the Hebrew has them here
decisions.reason: The verse keeps its own names, as the English; the meaning decision's footnote links them to verse 10.

decisions.choice: "Helem", "Hen"
decisions.reason: The names are kept as the Hebrew has them here; the meaning decision links them to Heldai and Josías of verse 10.

decisions.choice: "Helemu", "Heni"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names here differ from verse 10; Swahili keeps each as written, as the English does, and the meaning decision explains them.

decisions.choice: "헬렘" and "헨", as the Hebrew of this verse
decisions.reason: The verse names Heldai and Josiah differently from verse 10 (meaning decision); Korean keeps each verse's form, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And [those] far off will come and build in [the] temple of Yahweh, and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you. And it will be, if diligently you will listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God.

ko.L: 먼 곳에 있는 자들이 와서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전을 지을 것이다. 그러면 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알 것이다. 너희가 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 목소리를 정녕 듣기만 하면 [이 일이] 이루어질 것이다.
ko.B: 멀리 있는 사람들이 와서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 짓는 일을 도울 것이다. 그러면 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다. 너희가 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 성심으로 순종하면, 이 모든 일이 이루어질 것이다.
ko.R: 먼 곳에서 사람들이 와서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 짓는 일을 도울 것이다. 그러면 너희는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다. 너희가 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 정말로 순종하면, 이 모든 일이 일어날 것이다.

decisions.choice: those who are far off: Jews still in distant lands, and perhaps the nations
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the exiles still scattered abroad, like the men who brought gifts from Babylon (verse 10), or foreigners who will come to the LORD (2:15; 8:20-22; Isaiah 60:10). Either way, help for the temple will come from far away.

decisions.choice: if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God: the condition of Deuteronomy 28:1
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 28:1, where the blessings of the covenant depend on obedience. The sentence breaks off after "if", leaving the hearer to supply the blessing. The promises are sure, but the people's share in them depends on their obedience.

decisions.choice: you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me: the proof of the prophet's word
decisions.reason: The same assurance as in 2:13, 2:15 and 4:9.

decisions.choice: carefully obey (B); really obey (R)
alternatives: diligently listen to the voice of
decisions.reason: "Listen to the voice" means to obey, so Balanced and Readable say "obey", and add a word for the strengthening of the verb. Literal says "you shall know", as in 2:13.

decisions.choice: "si vous écoutez vraiment la voix" (L) for the doubled verb
decisions.reason: French renders the Hebrew infinitive plus verb with an adverb; Balanced and Readable say "obéir", as the English.

decisions.choice: "si escuchan atentamente la voz del SEÑOR su Dios"
decisions.reason: L keeps the wording of Deuteronomy 28:1 in Spanish ("si escuchas atentamente la voz del SEÑOR tu Dios"), here in the plural, so the allusion can be seen.

decisions.choice: the prophet speaks to the people with "các ngươi" and says "tôi" for himself
decisions.reason: The oracle's "các ngươi" carries on into the prophet's closing words, which are part of God's message, as in the term sheet.
